A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same frequency-domain analysis of momentum and the FSGDM optimizer. All 27 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification, IWSLT14 translation and MuJoCo reinforcement-learning results, plus momentum and hyperparameter analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Sections 3–5 and Appendix C, including accuracy tables, BLEU scores and reward curves.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same FSGDM momentum schedule, stage discretization, gradient scaling and parameter update. No proposed algorithm component, objective or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, ImageNet, IWSLT14 German-English translation, and the same three MuJoCo environments. The synthetic filtering demonstration and appendix test scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Standard-SGDM and EMA-SGDM remain the benchmark comparators. The alternative dynamic sequences and special momentum systems evaluated in the appendices also retain the same membership.

E3.justification: The reported models, training budgets, learning rates, batch sizes, preprocessing, evaluation metrics and RL testing schedule are unchanged. Experimental settings move from v1 Appendix C to v2 Appendix D without substantive revisions.

E4.justification: v1 Appendices B.1–B.9 match v2 C.1–C.9, retaining the dynamic-sequence comparisons, early-training analysis, special filters, extreme coefficients, optimal-zone studies and batch-size ablation. No distinct supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three-run means and standard errors for the relevant experiments, with seeds 0–2. RL retains ten seeds, 0–9, and 75% confidence intervals. No uncertainty-estimation or repeated-run reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–9 match, and the plotted results retain their values and trends. Figure 8(b) removes a duplicated FSGDM trace whose values match the retained trace; this is a display correction rather than a changed result.

T1.justification: The transfer-function analysis, magnitude and phase derivations, and training-length invariance proposition are unchanged. Phase-response material moves to Appendix A; Proposition 4.1 becomes Proposition 1, with its existing proof moving from Appendix A.3 to B.3.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion replace explicit generalization-performance assertions with less specific performance claims, modestly softening that framing. The frequency-domain framework, three empirical insights and claim that FSGDM outperforms conventional momentum optimizers remain.

C2.justification: v1 Appendix D tentatively suggests that the insights might apply to other optimizers; v2 Appendix E expresses a firmer belief that they do. Section 4.2 similarly changes a conjecture about similar filter responses yielding similar performance into an assumption. The unresolved obstacles to analyzing Adam remain explicit.

D1.justification: v1 promises code release upon publication; v2 states that the FSGDM implementation is available and supplies a repository link in footnote 1. This adds concrete access information. The documented implementation settings, hyperparameters and hardware otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes the Tieleman and Hinton (2012) RMSprop citation and reference when shortening the conclusion, although RMSprop remains discussed in the appendix. The other cited works and the central positioning relative to previous momentum research are retained.

P1.justification: The introduction, discussion and conclusion receive limited shortening and language edits. Phase-response discussion moves to a new Appendix A, with subsequent appendices renumbered. Author information and citation formatting also change, while the main narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted into ICLR style, changing typography, margins, headers and display placement throughout. The standalone title-and-abstract page becomes an integrated opening page, and figures and tables are resized and redistributed. Figure 8(b) also removes the duplicated FSGDM curve and legend entry.

improvement.justification: Replacing the future code-release promise with implementation access information, correcting Figure 8(b), and tightening the presentation provide limited gains in reproducibility information and clarity. The scientific evidence remains unchanged. The removed RMSprop citation and firmer unsupported extrapolation to adaptive optimizers are small countervailing edits.
